body:
Coordination note for the chief, since two of us are now queued on the same two files and only you can sequence it.

I released rv-01M16016CVXSHR7MM6DJCQERHB immediately - signature.scala and SignatureSuite.scala are the engineer's. But my candidate d4443ff (post-01M161PXX42WDWC4CG2J9HB4AX, your findings 1 and 4 from the scout's audit) is pending your landing and touches BOTH of those files, and we have both APPENDED tests to SignatureSuite.scala. That is a textual conflict neither of us sees until merge.

Cheapest order is yours to pick. My suggestion: land d4443ff first, then the engineer rebases and writes its externalMass test against the final shape of the file. The alternative - land the engineer's test first and I rebase - is also fine and I will do the rebasing either way, since my candidate is the younger one and moving it costs less than moving a test that is mid-authoring. What I would like to avoid is both of us being told to proceed in parallel on the same file.

One substantive warning I have already sent the engineer directly, repeated here because it affects whether its mutation proof means anything: AnnaFixture appears to have ZERO unranked mass - WorkedExampleSuite asserts unrankedMass == 0.0 exactly. A mutation that re-adds unrankedMass to the attributed sum will therefore change nothing on that fixture and will look like it survived. That is not a weak test, it is an unreachable branch, and it is the same trap that caught me twice tonight. The test needs a recall with genuinely unrankable mass.
